pro_course_detail.title: Read an article & discuss it with me!
pro_course_detail.description:
Objective: To improve reading skills, pronunciation, and comprehension through reading and discussing news articles.

Website: https://newsforkids.net/ (for A2-B1 students), https://www.npr.org/ (for B1-C2 students) or https://commonlit.org/en

Introduction: Welcome to the "Read an Article" lesson! In this lesson, you will have the opportunity to practice your reading skills, expand your vocabulary, and improve your pronunciation. 

Step 1: Article Selection
For A2-B1 students, we will be using the website https://newsforkids.net/ which provides interesting and age-appropriate news articles. B1-C2 students will have access to https://newsela.com/, a platform that offers articles at various reading levels to suit your proficiency. Select an article that interests you and make sure it is appropriate for your language level.

Step 2: Reading and Note-Taking
During the lesson, you will read the chosen article aloud while I listen attentively. As you read, I will type comments on Skype or in a shared document. These notes will help me identify areas for improvement in your pronunciation and comprehension.

Step 3: Pronunciation Practice
After you finish reading the article, we will focus on pronunciation. We will work together to correct any mispronunciations and ensure that you pronounce words accurately. To aid in this process, I will use phonetic symbols (/ˈsɪmblz/) to explain the correct pronunciation.

→ I will also write corrections in chat while you speak, and I will make suggestions about pronunciation, word choice, and grammar. 

Choose to practice your English! (`･ω･´)9

pro_course_detail.title: Discuss a specific topic with my PowerPoints (improve your English with topic-based lessons!)
pro_course_detail.description:
This is something you can use with any language. It's best to focus on 1 topic with a tutor. It's important to really "exhaust" the topic. For example, if you talk about the weather, talk about everything about the weather. Prepare for the lesson by learning vocabulary related to the topic, and then you try to talk about it for the entire session. If you pick "weather," you would talk about the weather today, the weather tomorrow and yesterday, the weather on vacation, how it's normally in May or December, how it's normally in Europe, the weather where you live, etc., and by the end of the session, you'll be very good at this topic, and you'll be able to express yourself just like any other native speaker. 

You can use one of my PowerPoints below. They include warm-up questions, pictures, questions, dialogue for 2 people to read, vocabulary practice, reading, etc. 

For upper beginner (20+ PowerPoints available):

Likes & dislikes, holiday food, computers, playing sports, snacks, food trucks, cooking methods,, family, fruits and vegetables, jobs in school, small talk, traveling, restaurants, in the airport, friendship, in the library, clothes, school, life in America

For intermediate (70+ PowerPoints available):

Dating, being alone, parenting, types of pets, feelings, police, cookies, vegetarian, going to the supermarket, kitchen equipment,  telephones, shopping online, birthdays, weather forecasts, barber and hair salon, restaurants, amusement parks, games

For intermediate-advanced (30+ PowerPoints available)

Greek food, water sports, tennis, donating plasma, colorblind, tornadoes, milk, Internet providers, Christmas tree, living in cities, body language, stuntmen, cat/dog breeds, paper quilling, gambling,  bicycles, celebrities, the library, food in South America

course_info.trial_description:
It usually feels very scary to book a first lesson. Maybe you have had bad experiences with English learning in the past. Perhaps it feels strange to meet a stranger on a computer. And of course - trying something new is always scary! And I'm a new person and learning English this way - may be a new thing for you! 

But please don't worry! You're not alone. Nearly EVERYONE feels this way. It was the same for me when I had my first online class. 

I will bring care and empathy to every lesson, and especially the first one. In the trial lesson, I won't be evaluating you. I will not correct your mistakes on our first call together. 

Instead - my intention is that you feel comfortable and relaxed. I want you to see what I am like as a teacher, and I want to get to know you! 

I know your abilities are better than they will appear in this first class, because you will probably be nervous. That's totally normal! We're humans! 

I will listen without judgement and offer a lot of empathy. I will let you speak. I will give you the opportunity to really be heard.

This will allow us to see if working together makes sense. If we decide to continue with another class, what you share in the trial lesson will help me design personalized classes for you - based on your interests, lifestyle needs, goals, strengths, and challenges. 

I hope this makes sense. If you don't understand anything, or if you have any questions - please message me!!!

I look forward to meeting you soon!

pro_course_detail.title: GETTING REAL: Conversations for people who don't like small talk
pro_course_detail.description:
For many people, even native English speakers, "small talk" is boring.

If you're learning English and you're someone who prefers to talk about deeper, more personal or meaningful topics -- small talk can be very unpleasant. 

I understand! That's how I feel. I don't like talking about the weather or what I did yesterday or what I am going to do for vacation/holiday.

Instead, I like to hear what people really think, what they have experienced in their lives, and what they care about.

I give students the opportunity to talk about what they LIKE to talk about. Things that interest them. What they like to think and learn about. Their lives. Their world. 

Getting a chance to actually converse, in English, might be just what you're missing - and it can help build your confidence and increase your motivation.

My students are usually people who like to learn - and outside of class they enjoy learning about psychology, philosophy, personal growth, art, creativity, entrepreneurship, and many other things. 

In our classes, I provide a space for students to talk about these topics - to engage with the material they watch or listen to. To share what they're learning and what it means to them. 

I hope you'll try out these classes - and tell me what you REALLY think! Let's engage in interesting conversations IN ENGLISH!
